mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month and 5-day forward returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases and 60-day forward returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM and 20-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases simultaneously, it indicates a strong labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously and 20-day forward returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases > 2% MoM and 5-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% in 1 month and 20-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows down by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year, it indicates stagflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth < -1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: If GDPC1 QoQ growth < -1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% simultaneously and 60-day forward returns are positive more than 50% of the time.
